title: English Question Tags and Subject-Verb Agreement Question Bank - Part 1
subject: English

questions.q: Everybody was watching the cricket match on TV, ______?
questions.subject: English
questions.explanation: 'Everybody' takes a plural pronoun ('they') and plural verb in the question tag. A positive statement requires a negative tag.

questions.q: He is a very wise man, ______?
questions.subject: English
questions.explanation: The statement is positive and uses the verb 'is', so the tag must be negative: 'isn't he'.

questions.q: Mrs Meena is a good teacher, ______?
questions.subject: English
questions.explanation: Positive statement with 'is' requires the negative tag 'isn't she'.

questions.q: We saw a rainbow in the sky, yesterday, ______?
questions.subject: English
questions.explanation: The main verb 'saw' is in the simple past tense, so the auxiliary 'did' is used in the negative tag: 'didn't we'.

questions.q: Sita is a beautiful girl, ______?
questions.subject: English
questions.explanation: Positive statement with 'is' requires the negative tag 'isn't she'.

questions.q: You should not smoke, ______?
questions.subject: English
questions.explanation: The statement is negative ('should not'), so the question tag must be positive: 'should you'.

questions.q: Miss Neha does not play tennis, ______?
questions.subject: English
questions.explanation: The statement is negative ('does not'), so the tag must be positive: 'does she'.

questions.q: I am older than you, ______?
questions.subject: English
questions.explanation: The standard question tag for 'I am' in a positive statement is 'aren't I'.

questions.q: You always have your lunch at 1 o'clock, ______?
questions.subject: English
questions.explanation: 'Have' is used here as a main verb (not an auxiliary), so the tag uses 'do': 'don't you'.

questions.q: I can do it for you, ______?
questions.subject: English
questions.explanation: Positive statement with modal 'can' requires the negative tag 'can't I'.

questions.q: She doesn't want to go to college today, ______?
questions.subject: English
questions.explanation: The statement is negative ('doesn't'), so the tag must be positive: 'does she'.

questions.q: Let's pray to Almighty, ______?
questions.subject: English
questions.explanation: Suggestions starting with 'Let's' always take the question tag 'shall we'.

questions.q: He had met you before, ______?
questions.subject: English
questions.explanation: The statement uses the past perfect auxiliary 'had', so the negative tag is 'hadn't he'.

questions.q: We couldn't enjoy the picnic, ______?
questions.subject: English
questions.explanation: The statement is negative ('couldn't'), so the tag must be positive: 'could we'.

questions.q: She was a teacher, ______?
questions.subject: English
questions.explanation: Positive statement with 'was' requires the negative tag 'wasn't she'.

questions.q: Tomorrow we will attend our college, ______?
questions.subject: English
questions.explanation: Positive statement with 'will' requires the negative tag 'won't we'.

questions.q: The Bishnois of Rajasthan protect trees and animals, ______?
questions.subject: English
questions.explanation: The main verb 'protect' is in the simple present tense, so the auxiliary 'do' is used in the negative tag: 'don't they'.

questions.q: Everyone wanted a ticket, ______?
questions.subject: English
questions.explanation: 'Everyone' takes a plural pronoun ('they') in the question tag. The past tense 'wanted' requires 'didn't'.

questions.q: Let's take a little rest before we start again, ______?
questions.subject: English
questions.explanation: Suggestions starting with 'Let's' always take the question tag 'shall we'.

questions.q: Anjali dances very well, ______?
questions.subject: English
questions.explanation: The main verb 'dances' is in the simple present tense, so the negative tag uses 'doesn't she'.

questions.q: Both Ram and Shyam are engineers, ______?
questions.subject: English
questions.explanation: Positive statement with 'are' and plural subject requires the negative tag 'aren't they'.

questions.q: He knows nobody in the colony, ______?
questions.subject: English
questions.explanation: 'Nobody' makes the statement negative, so the question tag must be positive: 'does he'.

questions.q: Jahangir was a great judge, ______?
questions.subject: English
questions.explanation: Positive statement with 'was' requires the negative tag 'wasn't he'.

questions.q: I am looking after the garden, ______?
questions.subject: English
questions.explanation: The standard question tag for 'I am' in a positive statement is 'aren't I'.

questions.q: It is quite hot outside today, ______?
questions.subject: English
questions.explanation: Positive statement with 'is' requires the negative tag 'isn't it'.

questions.q: Spot the error: (a) Neither of them / (b) are going to attend / (c) the party on 10th October. / (d) No error.
questions.subject: English
questions.explanation: 'Neither of them' is singular and requires a singular verb. 'are going' should be 'is going'.

questions.q: Spot the error: (a) He walked five miles which are really a great distance / (b) for a man like him who is not only old but also ill. / (c) No error / (d) No error.
options: He walked five miles which are really a great distance
for a man like him who is not only old but also ill.
questions.subject: English
questions.explanation: Distances, when considered as a single unit, take a singular verb. 'are really' should be 'is really'.

questions.q: Spot the error: (a) Either my colleague / (b) or a peon are coming home / (c) with the material today. / (d) No error.
options: or a peon are coming home
questions.subject: English
questions.explanation: With 'Either...or', the verb agrees with the subject nearest to it. 'a peon' is singular, so 'are coming' should be 'is coming'.

questions.q: Spot the error: (a) The rise and fall / (b) of the tide are due / (c) to lunar influence. / (d) No error.
questions.subject: English
questions.explanation: 'The rise and fall' refers to a single, compound idea (one phenomenon), so it takes a singular verb. 'are due' should be 'is due'.

questions.q: Spot the error: (a) Many a man / (b) have succumbed / (c) to this temptation. / (d) No error.
questions.subject: English
questions.explanation: 'Many a' is always followed by a singular noun and a singular verb. 'have succumbed' should be 'has succumbed'.

questions.q: Spot the error: (a) The introduction of tea, coffee / (b) and such other beverages / (c) have not been without some effect. / (d) No error.
options: have not been without some effect.
questions.subject: English
questions.explanation: The subject is 'The introduction' (singular), not 'beverages'. Therefore, 'have not been' should be 'has not been'.

questions.q: Spot the error: (a) The newer type of automatic machines / (b) wash / (c) clothes faster. / (d) No error.
options: The newer type of automatic machines
questions.subject: English
questions.explanation: The subject is 'type' (singular), so the verb must be singular. 'wash' should be 'washes'.

questions.q: Spot the error: (a) Each of the students in the computer class / (b) has to type / (c) their own research paper this semester. / (d) No error.
options: Each of the students in the computer class
their own research paper this semester.
questions.subject: English
questions.explanation: 'Each' is singular, so the possessive pronoun must also be singular. 'their' should be 'his or her'.

questions.q: Spot the error: (a) Everyone of the films / (b) you suggested / (c) are not worth seeing. / (d) No error.
questions.subject: English
questions.explanation: 'Every one' (two words) is singular and requires a singular verb. 'are not' should be 'is not'.

questions.q: Spot the error: (a) The Secretary and Principal of the college / (b) are attending / (c) the District Development Council Meeting at the Collectorate. / (d) No error.
options: The Secretary and Principal of the college
the District Development Council Meeting at the Collectorate.
questions.subject: English
questions.explanation: When two titles are joined by 'and' but share a single definite article ('The'), they refer to one person holding both posts. Thus, the verb must be singular: 'is attending'.

questions.q: Spot the error: (a) There is / (b) only one of his novels / (c) that are interesting. / (d) No error.
questions.subject: English
questions.explanation: The relative pronoun 'that' refers to 'one' (singular), so the verb must be singular. 'are interesting' should be 'is interesting'.

questions.q: Spot the error: (a) Knowledge of / (b) at least two languages / (c) are required to pass the examination. / (d) No error.
options: are required to pass the examination.
questions.subject: English
questions.explanation: The subject is 'Knowledge' (singular), so the verb must be singular. 'are required' should be 'is required'.

questions.q: Spot the error: (a) It is I / (b) who is to blame / (c) for this bad situation. / (d) No error.
questions.subject: English
questions.explanation: The relative pronoun 'who' refers to 'I', so the verb must agree with 'I'. 'is to blame' should be 'am to blame'.

questions.q: Spot the error: (a) Romanticism of melancholy / (b) in art and literature are the reason / (c) for insensitivity to those suffering from depression. / (d) No error.
options: in art and literature are the reason
for insensitivity to those suffering from depression.
questions.subject: English
questions.explanation: The subject is 'Romanticism' (singular), so the verb must be singular. 'are the reason' should be 'is the reason'.

questions.q: Spot the error: (a) Patience as well as perseverance / (b) are necessary / (c) for success. / (d) No error.
questions.subject: English
questions.explanation: When subjects are joined by 'as well as', the verb agrees with the first subject. 'Patience' is singular, so 'are necessary' should be 'is necessary'.

questions.q: Spot the error: (a) In Singapore / (b) my brother-in-law with his wife / (c) were present at the function. / (d) No error.
questions.subject: English
questions.explanation: Phrases like 'with his wife' do not change the number of the subject. 'brother-in-law' is singular, so 'were present' should be 'was present'.

questions.q: Spot the error: (a) A hot and / (b) a cold spring / (c) was found near each other. / (d) No error.
questions.subject: English
questions.explanation: The repetition of the article 'a' indicates two distinct springs. Therefore, the subject is plural, and 'was found' should be 'were found'.

questions.q: Spot the error: (a) Either of the roads / (b) lead / (c) to the park / (d) No error.
questions.subject: English
questions.explanation: 'Either' is singular and requires a singular verb. 'lead' should be 'leads'.

questions.q: Spot the error: (a) One of my desires / (b) are to become / (c) a doctor. / (d) No error.
questions.subject: English
questions.explanation: 'One' is the subject and is singular. 'are to become' should be 'is to become'.

questions.q: Spot the error: (a) The whole block of flats / (b) including two shops were / (c) destroyed in fire. / (d) No error.
questions.subject: English
questions.explanation: The subject is 'block' (singular). Phrases starting with 'including' do not change the number. 'were' should be 'was'.

questions.q: Spot the error: (a) The sum and substance / (b) of his poem / (c) are as follows. / (d) No error.
questions.subject: English
questions.explanation: 'The sum and substance' is a hendiadys (a single idea expressed by two words) and takes a singular verb. 'are' should be 'is'.

questions.q: Spot the error: (a) Neither of the / (b) five accused / (c) could be convicted. / (d) No error.
questions.subject: English
questions.explanation: The sentence is grammatically correct. 'Neither of' takes a singular concept, and the modal 'could' does not change form for number.

questions.q: Spot the error: (a) The strain of all / (b) the difficulties, vexations and anxieties / (c) were more than he could beat. / (d) No error.
options: were more than he could beat.
questions.subject: English
questions.explanation: The subject is 'strain' (singular). 'were' should be 'was'.

questions.q: Spot the error: (a) Everybody / (b) it must be admitted / (c) has their ups and downs. / (d) No error.
questions.subject: English
questions.explanation: 'Everybody' is singular, so the possessive pronoun must be singular. 'their' should be 'his or her'.

questions.q: Spot the error: (a) Every woman in the world / (b) fervently hopes that their child / (c) will be a normal and healthy baby / (d) No error.
options: will be a normal and healthy baby
questions.subject: English
questions.explanation: 'Every woman' is singular, so the possessive pronoun must be singular. 'their' should be 'her'.

questions.q: Spot the error: (a) Neither of them / (b) sent their papers / (c) in time for the last seminar / (d) No error.
options: in time for the last seminar
questions.subject: English
questions.explanation: 'Neither' is singular, so the possessive pronoun must be singular. 'their' should be 'his or her'.

questions.q: Spot the error: (a) This is a strange world / (b) where each one pursues their own golden bubble / (c) and laughs at others for doing the same. / (d) No error.
options: where each one pursues their own golden bubble
and laughs at others for doing the same.
questions.subject: English
questions.explanation: 'Each one' is singular, so the possessive pronoun must be singular. 'their' should be 'his or her'.

questions.q: Spot the error: (a) If it were possible to get near when / (b) one of the volcanic eruptions take place / (c) we would see a grand sight. / (d) No error.
options: If it were possible to get near when
one of the volcanic eruptions take place
we would see a grand sight.
questions.subject: English
questions.explanation: 'One' is the subject and is singular. 'take place' should be 'takes place'.

questions.q: Spot the error: (a) A rise in rents and wages / (b) have been found / (c) to go together. / (d) No error.
options: A rise in rents and wages
questions.subject: English
questions.explanation: The subject is 'A rise' (singular). 'have been found' should be 'has been found'.

questions.q: Spot the error: (a) He is one of those few post-colonial writer who believes / (b) that this talk about colonialism has gone too far / (c) and has turned into a cliche. / (d) No error.
options: He is one of those few post-colonial writer who believes
that this talk about colonialism has gone too far
and has turned into a cliche.
questions.subject: English
questions.explanation: 'One of those' must be followed by a plural noun. 'writer' should be 'writers', and consequently 'believes' should be 'believe'.
